findings.evidence:
- Scenario2 non-null check changed to FD-based: `pkg/planner/core/rule/rule_outer_join_to_semi_join.go:271-285` uses `innerChild.ExtractFD().NotNullCols.Has(isNullCol.UniqueID)` instead of `mysql.HasNotNullFlag`.
- Outer-join FD extraction treats join predicates as “filters” for not-null extraction: `pkg/planner/core/operator/logicalop/logical_join.go:916-952` builds `allConds` including `EqualConditions`/`OtherConditions`, runs `util.ExtractNotNullFromConds(allConds, p)`, then `filterFD.MakeNotNull(...)`.
- Not-null extraction marks *all referenced columns* of any null-rejected predicate as NOT NULL: `pkg/planner/util/funcdep_misc.go:24-50`.
- Outer-join FD merge keeps those NOT NULL markings for outer-side cols (only subtracts `innerCols`): `pkg/planner/funcdep/fd_graph.go:854-857`.
- In null-reject-check folding, functions with a NULL constant arg can fold to NULL even if other args aren’t constant: `pkg/expression/constant_fold.go:191-222`, making `IsNullRejected` true for many join predicates.
findings.fix: Keep Scenario2 semantics “DDL NOT NULL, but not made nullable by outer joins” by gating FD-not-null with schema NOT NULL, e.g. require both `mysql.HasNotNullFlag(innerSch.Columns[idx].RetType.GetFlag())` and `fds.NotNullCols.Has(int(isNullCol.UniqueID))` (or otherwise restrict FD-based acceptance to cases that cannot be satisfied solely via join-predicate null-rejection inside an innerChild outer join).
findings.impact:
Potential wrong results: Scenario2 may become true for columns that are nullable in `innerChild` output (especially when `innerChild` is an outer-join subtree), causing `OuterJoinToSemiJoin` to rewrite an outer join into an anti-semi join and drop matched rows that legitimately satisfy `IS NULL` due to actual NULL values.

Example shape that can be mis-rewritten:
`SELECT ... FROM t1 LEFT JOIN (t2 LEFT JOIN t3 ON t2.i = t3.i) s ON s.j = t1.a WHERE s.i IS NULL;`
If `t2.i` is nullable and some matched `t2` row has `i IS NULL`, original query keeps that matched row; anti-semi rewrite would exclude it because a match exists.
findings.verify: Add a planner case test where the `IS NULL` column is nullable and comes from the outer side of a nested outer join, while the *top* outer join matches on a different (non-null) column. Assert the plan keeps `Selection isnull(...)` and does not rewrite the top join to `AntiSemiJoin`, and assert result includes a matched row with `inner_col IS NULL`.
findings.what: Scenario2 now uses FD-derived `NotNullCols` as a proxy for “inner column is NOT NULL”, but FD not-null can be inferred from null-rejecting join predicates inside an `innerChild` outer join even when the column can still be NULL in `innerChild` output. This can incorrectly enable outer-join→anti-semi rewrites and change SQL semantics.

subject: planner: fix outer-join-to-anti-semi rewrite for nested outer joins (#65749)
summary: Commit fixes the reported nested-outer-join case by switching Scenario2’s NOT NULL check to FD-derived not-null info. However, using `ExtractFD().NotNullCols` as the sole Scenario2 gate can misclassify nullable columns (notably from outer-join subtrees) as NOT NULL, potentially enabling incorrect anti-semi rewrites and wrong query results. No follow-up fix found up to `upstream/master`.
